answer.rationale: p99 latency spike (5x target) coincides temporally with release 2 hours ago. memory_b1 demonstrates rollback as an effective tool for checkout error spikes with no customer impact. memory_b6 shows staged gating can miss regressions that still reach prod. Current situation has writes at peak during settlement—memory_b2 warns against failover during hot writes, which makes rollback safer than regional move. Verifying memory_b1 (prior stable build rollback success) and memory_b2 (replication/failover risks during writes) to confirm rollback is lower-risk than failover. Rolling back to prior stable build isolates whether the release caused latency and pauses any bad code while preserving write consistency. This is the single intervention we can execute now without cascade risk.
